name: player
description: A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking.
readmeExcerpt:
A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking. A few lines of code put a character in a page, a stream overlay or an app.
Comes with 25 featured characters in different styles, ready to use.

English · 中文 · 日本語 · Tiếng Việt

- WebGL2, no dependencies, about 30 KB gzipped for the core - Lip sync (microphone, audio, video) and webcam face tracking (MediaPipe), both in the browser, imported only when you need them - Plays LivLiv, VRM and PNGTuber characters through the same API - Full-body characters stand on the ground: they sway, crouch and dip with their feet in place, in the shot you pick - 25 featured characters in [`characters/`](characters/), ready to use ## Try it - **Online**: the examples run on [livliv-dev.github.io/player](https://livliv-dev.github.io/player/). - **Here**: `npm install && npm run build`, serve this folder with any static server and open `/example/demo.html` (expressions, actions, microphone, camera; `?model=../characters//` picks another character). `/example/png.html` and `/example/vrm.html` show a PNGTuber and a VRM. - **On livliv.ai**: each character's page there plays it with the same renderer. Start at [livliv.ai/discover](https://livliv.ai/discover). ## Project LivLiv We want the art of creating characters to belong to everyone. We're open-sourcing our AI tools for character creation, [the player and its playback protocol](https://github.com/livliv-dev/player), and [a stage where your characters can meet an audience](https://github.com/livliv-dev/stage). Come say hello on [Discord](https://discord.gg/ac5qF36T2H) and follow us on [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/livliv_ai). ## Use it in your page ```sh npm install @livliv-dev/player ``` ```js import { Player } from '@livliv-dev/player' const player = new Player(document.querySelector('canvas')) await player.load('characters/k01/') // a folder with model.json and textures/, or a .livliv file player.setExpression('smile') // ids are in player.expressions player.act('nod') player.params.mouthOpen = 0.6 // 0..1 ``` Lip sync and face tracking: ```js import { createSpeech } from '@livliv-dev/player/voice' import { startFaceTracking } from '@livliv-dev/player/tracking' // needs @mediapipe/tasks-vision const speech = createSpeech(player) button.onclick = () => { speech.unlock(); speech.say('/reply.mp3') } await startFaceTracking(player) ``` A VRM or a PNGTuber, on the same API: ```js import { BodyPlayer } from '@livliv-dev/player/body' import { VrmBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/vrm' // needs three and @pixiv/three-vrm import { PngBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/png' const vrm = new BodyPlayer(canvasA, new VrmBody()) await vrm.load('/avatars/me.vrm') const png = new BodyPlayer(canvasB, new PngBody()) await png.load({ closed: 'me-closed.png', open: 'me-open.png' }) ``` The whole API is in [API.md](API.md): options, params, expressions and actions, drivers, recorded poses and attachment points, VRM and PNGTuber characters, the limits on untrusted files, the model package and the format version. The LivLiv package format (`.livliv`, `model.json` v4) is in [FORMAT.md](FORMAT.md), with a JSON Schema in [`schema/`](schema/); packages exported before v4 are described in [FORMAT-v3.md](FORMAT-v3.md) and still play. > The npm package is the player alone. The featured characters are in this repository's [`characters/`](characters/): copy > the ones you use next to your page, with their licence. ## Featured characters `characters/` holds 25 characters, ready to `load()`. Most were made by LivLiv: use them free with credit ("Characters: LivLiv (livliv.ai)"), commercially too if you are an individual. Don't sell them or merchandise made from them, and don't train AI models on them. They are **not** covered by the Apache License; the terms are in [characters/LICENSE.md](characters/LICENSE.md). Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen come from other people's work, with their own terms in [characters/CREDITS.md](characters/CREDITS.md). **New in 0.5.0: full-body characters.** Drawn head to feet, they stand on the ground: they sway, crouch and dip while their feet stay put. Four featured characters are full-body: Tsubaki, Neve, Juno and Viola (f05–f08). Pick the shot with `player.view.fit`: `'frame'` (default), `'knee'` or `'whole'`; see [Full-body characters](API.md#full-body-characters) in API.md. Each character has a `cover.webp`, its first frame: `player.load(source, { poster })` shows it until the character is ready, and [example/loading.js](example/loading.js) shows it before any script has run. Each character is also one file to download, `.livliv`, at `https://livliv-dev.github.io/player/characters/.livliv` (the names below link to them). They are served with CORS, so a page on another site can `load()` one straight from there, and [`index.json`](https://livliv-dev.github.io/player/characters/index.json) lists them all. | id | name | of your own from one picture on [livliv.ai](https://livliv.ai). - **A PNGTuber**: two pictures (mouth closed, mouth open), and two more with the eyes closed if you have them. - **A VRM**: from VRoid Studio or any tool that exports VRM 0.x or 1.0. - **A LivLiv model**: make one from a picture on [livliv.ai](https://livliv.ai), then download its model package from the character's page (**Model package**): a `.livliv` file. Pass it to `load()` as it is (a URL, or the `File` someone picked), or unzipped as a folder. Full-body characters play too (from 0.5); livliv.ai does not offer their packages yet. ## About the player and the characters LivLiv Player and the `.livliv` format are LivLiv's own work. They use no Live2D software or Cubism SDK and do not read `.moc3` or `.cmo3` files. "Live2D" is a trademark of Live2D Inc.; LivLiv is not affiliated with it. Making a character on livliv.ai uses AI. The player itself only plays: it calls no AI service and reads only the files you point it at. Face tracking runs Google's MediaPipe in the browser, and camera images stay on the device; API.md has the networking details. The featured characters in this repository were made on LivLiv too, also with AI; Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen adapt other people's characters ([credits](characters/CREDITS.md)). Refined Nana (`d03ft`) also has swinging parts and head-turn keyforms added with LivLiv's own tools. A package's `meta.author` and `meta.license` record who made it and on what terms: keep them and follow them. When you show a character made with LivLiv in public, say that AI was used to make it, and don't present it as hand-drawn or hand-rigged. ## Embed without code ```html ``` The same `/live/` page has a transparent background and works as an OBS Browser Source.\ (Powered by [https://livliv.ai](https://livliv.ai)) ## Develop ```sh git clone https://github.com/livliv-dev/player cd player npm install npm run check # types npm run build # dist/: index.js, tracking.js, voice.js, body.js, png.js, vrm.js (ES modules), chunks/ and types/ npm test # unit and fuzz tests (Node 22.18 or newer, no browser) npm run test:browser # every featured character drawn in headless Chromium; once: npx playwright-core install chromium-headless-shell npm run test:engines # a sample on Firefox and WebKit, where WebGL2 starts (a GPU or a software GL); once: npx playwright-core install firefox webkit ``` `src/runtime/` is the renderer and motion code livliv.ai runs; this repository is published from it. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Security reports: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Browser support WebGL2 and ES2023: Chrome / Edge 97+, Firefox 104+, Safari 15.4+. Tested on current desktop browsers, not yet on phones. ## License The code is under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE) (see also [NOTICE](NOTICE)). releases.name: LivLiv Player 0.5.1
releases.body:
Two optional settings for how strongly a character moves. A page that doesn't use them draws exactly as with 0.5.0.

### New

- `act(action, strength)`: a short move at a share of its full size, from 0 to 1 (default 1). It takes as long as
  before. See [API.md](https://github.com/livliv-dev/player/blob/main/API.md#motion-strength).
- `bodyMotion` (0 to 1, default 1): scales the live torso turn and lean, before `parameterProfile`. Recorded poses
  already include it, so replaying them doesn't scale them again.
- The repository's featured characters now include four full-body ones: Tsubaki, Neve, Juno and Viola.

### Changed

- The package builds itself when it is installed straight from GitHub (`prepare` instead of `prepack`), so
  `npm install github:livliv-dev/player#<commit>` gives a working copy.

```bash
npm install @livliv-dev/player@0.5.1
```

releases.name: LivLiv Player 0.5.0
releases.body:
Full-body characters, standing on the ground, with a choice of shot. Half-body characters draw exactly as in 0.4, and a
page written for 0.4 needs no change.

### New

- **Full-body characters**, livliv.ai's newer kind: drawn head to feet, the feet on the ground. The upper body moves as a
  half-body character's; the whole figure sways from the ankles, the hips shift their weight, a skirt's or coat's hem
  trails behind; leaning toward the camera or a hop crouches it, a hop lands, and lip sync dips the upper body. See
  [API.md](https://github.com/livliv-dev/player/blob/main/API.md#full-body-characters).
- **Choose the shot** with `view.fit`: `'frame'` (head and chest, the default), `'knee'` or `'whole'`.
- **For drivers and recordings:** `ModelInfo.fullBody`, `frame.talk` (the talking bob, apart from `frame.move`),
  `frame.grounded` and the `Fit` type. A full-body character's `PlaybackPose` keeps `crouch`, `dip` and `talk`, and
  `renderPose()` draws them again.
- **Format 4.1** ([FORMAT.md](https://github.com/livliv-dev/player/blob/main/FORMAT.md#full-body-characters-41)):

releases.name: LivLiv Player 0.4.0
releases.body:
Ways to record a character and show it in more than one place, and two changes to what a character does: the chest
spring is off, and full-body characters wait for a later version. A page written for 0.3 needs no change.

### New

- Recorded poses: `getPose()`, `onFrame` and `renderPose(pose, dt, size)` on `Player` and `BodyPlayer`, to keep each
  frame's pose and draw it again, in another window or at a video's exact size. See [API.md](API.md#recorded-poses).
- `renderWhenHidden`: keep drawing while the canvas is out of view, for a live output or a recording.
- Response profiles, which reshape params one by one (range, curve, smoothing): `parameterProfile` and
  `parameterSample` on both players, `profile` and `sample` on face tracking, and `TrackingFilter`,
  `readTrackingProfile()`, `parameterRule()` and `TRACKING_PARAMETERS` from `@livliv-dev/player/tracking`. See
  [API.md](API.md#response-profiles).
- `getAnchor('head' | 'body')`: where the head and the torso were drawn, to attach things that follow the character. A
  `Body` of your own can give its own with `anchor()`.
- Face tracking: `deviceId` picks the camera, and `tracking.video` is its preview.

releases.name: LivLiv Player 0.3.0
releases.body:
The first version of LivLiv Player on npm. The interface settled first, so a page written for 0.2 needs a few changes. Format 4 is unchanged.

## What to change from 0.2

| 0.2 | 0.3 |
|---|---|
| `import ... from '@livliv/player'` and its subpaths | `'@livliv-dev/player'`, the package's name on npm. |
| `player.act('away')` | `player.setAway(true)` and `setAway(false)`. `act('away')` now throws: it was a switch among one-off moves. |
| `player.puppet` | No longer in the types. `player.poke()` and `player.canvasToModel()` are what pages used it for. The field still exists and can change in any version. |
| `player.load(a); player.load(b)` played `a`, then `b` | The new load replaces the one running, which rejects with an `AbortError`. If you catch errors, let this one through: `if (e.name === 'AbortError') return`. |
| `dispose()` on a load running rejected with an `Error` | It rejects with an `AbortError`, as `load()` on a disposed player does. |
| Errors told apart by their message | `e.code`, on a `LivLivError`. The messages can change. |

## Install

```sh
npm install @livliv-dev/player
```

readmeHtml:
A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking. A few lines of code put a character in a page, a stream overlay or an app.
Comes with 25 featured characters in different styles, ready to use.

English · 中文 · 日本語 · Tiếng Việt

  • WebGL2, no dependencies, about 30 KB gzipped for the core
  • Lip sync (microphone, audio, video) and webcam face tracking (MediaPipe), both in the browser, imported only when you need them
  • Plays LivLiv, VRM and PNGTuber characters through the same API
  • Full-body characters stand on the ground: they sway, crouch and dip with their feet in place, in the shot you pick
  • 25 featured characters in characters/, ready to use

Try it

  • Online: the examples run on livliv-dev.github.io/player.
  • Here: npm install && npm run build, serve this folder with any static server and open /example/demo.html (expressions, actions, microphone, camera; ?model=../characters/<id>/ picks another character). /example/png.html and /example/vrm.html show a PNGTuber and a VRM.
  • On livliv.ai: each character's page there plays it with the same renderer. Start at livliv.ai/discover.

Project LivLiv

We want the art of creating characters to belong to everyone.

We're open-sourcing our AI tools for character creation, the player and its playback protocol, and a stage where your characters can meet an audience.

Come say hello on Discord and follow us on X (Twitter).

Use it in your page

npm install @livliv-dev/player
import { Player } from '@livliv-dev/player'

const player = new Player(document.querySelector('canvas'))
await player.load('characters/k01/')   // a folder with model.json and textures/, or a .livliv file

player.setExpression('smile')          // ids are in player.expressions
player.act('nod')
player.params.mouthOpen = 0.6          // 0..1

Lip sync and face tracking:

import { createSpeech } from '@livliv-dev/player/voice'
import { startFaceTracking } from '@livliv-dev/player/tracking'   // needs @mediapipe/tasks-vision

const speech = createSpeech(player)
button.onclick = () => { speech.unlock(); speech.say('/reply.mp3') }

await startFaceTracking(player)

A VRM or a PNGTuber, on the same API:

import { BodyPlayer } from '@livliv-dev/player/body'
import { VrmBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/vrm'    // needs three and @pixiv/three-vrm
import { PngBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/png'

const vrm = new BodyPlayer(canvasA, new VrmBody())
await vrm.load('/avatars/me.vrm')
const png = new BodyPlayer(canvasB, new PngBody())
await png.load({ closed: 'me-closed.png', open: 'me-open.png' })

The whole API is in API.md: options, params, expressions and actions, drivers, recorded poses and attachment points, VRM and PNGTuber characters, the limits on untrusted files, the model package and the format version. The LivLiv package format (.livliv, model.json v4) is in FORMAT.md, with a JSON Schema in schema/; packages exported before v4 are described in FORMAT-v3.md and still play.

The npm package is the player alone. The featured characters are in this repository's characters/: copy the ones you use next to your page, with their licence.

Featured characters

characters/ holds 25 characters, ready to load(). Most were made by LivLiv: use them free with credit ("Characters: LivLiv (livliv.ai)"), commercially too if you are an individual. Don't sell them or merchandise made from them, and don't train AI models on them. They are not covered by the Apache License; the terms are in characters/LICENSE.md. Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen come from other people's work, with their own terms in characters/CREDITS.md.

New in 0.5.0: full-body characters. Drawn head to feet, they stand on the ground: they sway, crouch and dip while their feet stay put. Four featured characters are full-body: Tsubaki, Neve, Juno and Viola (f05–f08). Pick the shot with player.view.fit: 'frame' (default), 'knee' or 'whole'; see Full-body characters in API.md.

Each character has a cover.webp, its first frame: player.load(source, { poster }) shows it until the character is ready, and example/loading.js shows it before any script has run.

Each character is also one file to download, <id>.livliv, at https://livliv-dev.github.io/player/characters/<id>.livliv (the names below link to them). They are served with CORS, so a page on another site can load() one straight from there, and index.json lists them all.

id name id name id name
k01 Sena d01 Yui v01 Aster
k02 Elio d02 Leo v03 Mira
char06 Aoi d03 Nana v04 Kai
char07 Sora d03ft Nana (refined) v05 Lilith
s01 Hana p01 Kujira v06 Usa
q02 Mochi p02 Kujira Q v07 Stella
q03 Kotaro p03 Pen w01 Max
f05 Tsubaki (full-body) f06 Neve (full-body) f07 Juno (full-body)
f08 Viola (full-body)

Characters of your own

You can bring in a PNGTuber's pictures, or a VRM (drawn with three.js); or make a character of your own from one picture on livliv.ai.

  • A PNGTuber: two pictures (mouth closed, mouth open), and two more with the eyes closed if you have them.
  • A VRM: from VRoid Studio or any tool that exports VRM 0.x or 1.0.
  • A LivLiv model: make one from a picture on livliv.ai, then download its model package from the character's page (Model package): a .livliv file. Pass it to load() as it is (a URL, or the File someone picked), or unzipped as a folder. Full-body characters play too (from 0.5); livliv.ai does not offer their packages yet.

About the player and the characters

LivLiv Player and the .livliv format are LivLiv's own work. They use no Live2D software or Cubism SDK and do not read .moc3 or .cmo3 files. "Live2D" is a trademark of Live2D Inc.; LivLiv is not affiliated with it.

Making a character on livliv.ai uses AI. The player itself only plays: it calls no AI service and reads only the files you point it at. Face tracking runs Google's MediaPipe in the browser, and camera images stay on the device; API.md has the networking details.

The featured characters in this repository were made on LivLiv too, also with AI; Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen adapt other people's characters (credits). Refined Nana (d03ft) also has swinging parts and head-turn keyforms added with LivLiv's own tools.

A package's meta.author and meta.license record who made it and on what terms: keep them and follow them. When you show a character made with LivLiv in public, say that AI was used to make it, and don't present it as hand-drawn or hand-rigged.

Embed without code

<iframe src="https://livliv.ai/live/k01" width="480" height="640" allow="camera; microphone"
  style="border:0;background:transparent"></iframe>

The same /live/<id> page has a transparent background and works as an OBS Browser Source.
(Powered by https://livliv.ai)

Develop

git clone https://github.com/livliv-dev/player
cd player
npm install
npm run check          # types
npm run build          # dist/: index.js, tracking.js, voice.js, body.js, png.js, vrm.js (ES modules), chunks/ and types/
npm test               # unit and fuzz tests (Node 22.18 or newer, no browser)
npm run test:browser   # every featured character drawn in headless Chromium; once: npx playwright-core install chromium-headless-shell
npm run test:engines   # a sample on Firefox and WebKit, where WebGL2 starts (a GPU or a software GL); once: npx playwright-core install firefox webkit

src/runtime/ is the renderer and motion code livliv.ai runs; this repository is published from it. See CONTRIBUTING.md. Security reports: SECURITY.md.

Browser support

WebGL2 and ES2023: Chrome / Edge 97+, Firefox 104+, Safari 15.4+. Tested on current desktop browsers, not yet on phones.

License

The code is under the Apache License 2.0 (see also NOTICE). The featured characters have their own licence, characters/LICENSE.md. You may keep the LivLiv name and logo in your own versions, as long as they don't claim to be the official one.

Thanks

Thanks to 上善无形, ZipZipPipe and 贱兔死顺盖, whose characters Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen are based on: see characters/CREDITS.md.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Customizable, lightweight HTML5 video player component.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This project provides a modern HTML5 video player focused on performance and customizability. It offers a clean default UI while allowing extensive styling via CSS variables. The player handles common media events and provides a simplified API for playback control. It is built without heavy dependencies to ensure fast load times. The architecture supports plugins for adding features like analytics or ads.
keyFeatures: Customizable UI: allows complete restyling of controls using CSS variables.
Plugin system: supports extending functionality with modular JavaScript plugins.
Event handling: normalizes HTML5 media events into a consistent API.
Keyboard accessibility: includes built-in support for standard keyboard shortcuts.
Responsive design: adapts automatically to different screen sizes and orientations.

useCases.title: Custom Media Platforms
useCases.description: Build branded video experiences without relying on generic iframes.

useCases.title: Lightweight Embedding
useCases.description: Embed videos on landing pages with minimal impact on load times.

useCases.title: Interactive Video
useCases.description: Extend the player with custom overlays or interactive elements.

useCases.title: Accessible Playback
useCases.description: Ensure video content is navigable via keyboard and screen readers.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend developers building custom video experiences on the web. It is ideal for projects that require a player lighter and more flexible than standard libraries.
